subject.title: feat(feeds): expose publisher follow gateway RPCs

question: Should signed publisher-feed following become a core OpenClaw Gateway, CLI, scheduler, and shared-state capability, or remain an optional ClawHub/plugin-owned integration?
rationale: The branch adds permanent public contracts, recurring network behavior, a configured signing-trust boundary, and shared persistent state; repository policy cannot resolve that ownership choice without explicit product intent.

options.title: Pause for core sponsorship
options.body: Keep the stack open but do not merge until a maintainer explicitly accepts the core ownership, trust model, persistence contract, and rollout plan.

options.title: Move to a plugin
options.body: Rework publisher following as an optional plugin or ClawHub package and add only a narrowly proven generic core seam if the current plugin APIs are insufficient.

options.title: Approve core with gates
options.body: Accept the core direction after the contributor adds public docs, live proof, and fresh-install plus upgrade evidence for the shared SQLite and scheduled-service changes.

recommendation.title: Pause for core sponsorship
recommendation.body: Keep the stack open but do not merge until a maintainer explicitly accepts the core ownership, trust model, persistence contract, and rollout plan.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice changes OpenClaw's core product boundary and long-lived Gateway and storage contracts.
